finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in /dl allows arbitrary file read outside /srv/files via the f query parameter.
finding.source: r.URL.Query().Get("f") at files.go:12, unauthenticated GET /dl route registered at files.go:32
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13; response written at files.go:18

trace.note: name taken verbatim from query parameter f
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd; Join lexically resolves .. with no containment check
os.ReadFile opens the resolved path and follows symlinks
file contents written to the HTTP response with no content-type restriction

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Clean plus prefix check against root; no os.Root or EvalSymlinks containment; no rejection of .. or absolute input; no authentication, authorization, or middleware on /dl; NotFound branch only handles read errors

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12 takes f verbatim; files.go:13 is a bare filepath.Join + os.ReadFile with no Clean-and-prefix check, no os.Root, and no ".."/absolute rejection; files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth or middleware; the err branch at files.go:14-16 only returns NotFound on read failure. The avatar handler's filepath.Base at files.go:22 is not applied to /dl.
verdict.reason: The trace holds: at files.go:13, f="../../etc/passwd" resolves via filepath.Join to /etc/passwd, which os.ReadFile opens and files.go:18 writes to the response, and the unauthenticated route at files.go:32 lets anonymous clients reach it, so no effective control blocks it. The finding's "symlinks" note is extraneous but does not change the result.

finding.claim: /dl has no authorization, so every file under /srv/files is readable by any unauthenticated caller; a design-dependent authorization gap.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile at files.go:13 via the /dl handler

trace.note: /dl registered directly with http.HandleFunc, no auth wrapper
handler accepts no identity or ownership input
any file under root is read for any caller

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, per-user ownership check, or access-control list anywhere in the file. Severity depends on whether the directory is intended to be public.

verdict.guard_found: none. /dl is registered directly at files.go:32 with no auth wrapper, and download() (files.go:11-19) reads no identity or ownership data. The only input handling is r.URL.Query().Get("f") at files.go:12, which is passed to os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13 with no check that the result stays under root. The only sanitizer in the file, filepath.Base, is applied to /avatar at files.go:22, not to /dl.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: /dl is registered unauthenticated at files.go:32, and download() at files.go:11-13 passes the caller's f parameter straight into os.ReadFile with no auth or containment check, so any anonymous client on :8082 can read files. The candidate understates the impact: because filepath.Join cleans the path, f=../../etc/passwd escapes /srv/files, so this is a path traversal as well as a missing authorization check, and it is a real vulnerability regardless of whether /srv/files is meant to be public.
